_comment: Red-flag rules for score.py. Written from the Gold Coast criteria (Shefner 2020) and the red flags of ALS Canada's ReferALS tool as summarised in the R.A.C.E. to Diagnose ALS/MND handout. Frozen before any test case was seen. Edit numbers and wording here, no code changes needed. 'when' is the finding's value that earns the points (true or false).
_sources: Shefner JM et al. A proposal for new diagnostic criteria for ALS (Gold Coast criteria). Clin Neurophysiol 2020;131:1975-1978.
ALS Canada. ReferALS early referral tool. als.ca/resource/referals-early-referral-tool
R.A.C.E. to Diagnose ALS/MND participant handout (adapted from ReferALS): 'If it's progressive and doesn't fit - REFER'; 'progressive, painless loss of function'. als-mnd.org

rules.why: Weakness is painless (ReferALS: 'progressive, painless loss of function')
No numbness or tingling (ALS spares sensation)
Numbness or tingling points to a nerve or root problem instead
Fasciculations, visible twitching (lower motor neuron sign)
Up-going plantar or Hoffmann sign (upper motor neuron sign)
Sensory nerves test normal despite weakness
Getting worse despite treatment for a local cause
Speech or swallowing change (bulbar red flag)
Breathing change, e.g. short of breath lying flat (respiratory red flag)

unexplained_why: Doesn't fit: weakness and wasting with normal sensory nerve tests, so carpal tunnel or a pinched nerve does not explain it
spread_why: Weakness has spread to a second region
umn_plus_lmn_why: Upper and lower motor neuron signs together
_gold_coast: Risk is 'high' whatever the points if: UMN sign (brisk reflexes / up-going plantar / Hoffmann) AND LMN sign (wasting / fasciculations) AND getting worse (spread or failed local treatment).

advice.high: Refer to neurology (ALS / motor neuron disease clinic) now. Write 'progressive, painless loss of function' on the referral. Do not wait for more tests or treatment trials.
advice.medium: Possible early pattern. Re-examine within 4 to 6 weeks; refer to neurology if weakness spreads, wasting appears, or treatment does not help.
advice.low: No ALS red-flag pattern in these notes.
